phase: P1 typed wire bridge (Plan 04) + baseline eval (Plan 08)
note: Written and committed BEFORE the first baseline run. A tolerance edited after seeing the numbers is a rationalization, not a criterion (Plan 08 §0). `first_run_at` is set by the run commit and never by this one; a tolerance loosened here after that date is refused by shell/tests/eval-preregistration.test.ts.

bounds_recorded_at_preregistration: The corpus table in the fixture is truncated to 99 characters per row, while tests/eval.rs DOCS carries the untruncated sentences. The baseline seeds the fixture's OWN corpus (the frozen artifact Plan 08 §1 names), so its numbers are not comparable to an in-process run over eval.rs DOCS. Recorded, not repaired: the fixture is frozen.

tests/eval.rs QUERIES holds 107 queries; the fixture holds 106. The extra one is `SnapSync`, a negation probe with an EMPTY relevant set. The fixture therefore carries exactly one negation probe (`Kubernetes ingress`). The runner reads the FIXTURE, so the baseline covers 106 queries. Recorded, not repaired.

Corpus rows are truncated, so gold answers that depend on a truncated tail (doc 9's 'four percent of global revenue') are only partially matchable. This lowers the achievable ceiling and is part of why T5 is recorded rather than gated.

T1_wire_lossless.rule: For every judged query, the ordered hit-id sequence the shell's typed recall path returns MUST equal the ordered hit-id sequence the same kernel returns for the same request over plain HTTP POST /recall. Divergence in ANY position is a bridge defect.
T1_wire_lossless.decides_in_advance: Attribution. If the two sequences differ, the conclusion is 'the bridge loses, duplicates, or reorders rows' — never 'recall@k moved'. Retrieval quality and wire losslessness are measured separately so neither can absorb the other.
T1_wire_lossless.compares: ordered id sequences (positional), never a count or a total

T2_decision_complete.rule: Every shaped response carries a `decision`, and every value is a member of the published enum. 0 responses without `decision`; 0 values outside {ok, low_confidence}.
T2_decision_complete.decides_in_advance: A response missing `decision` VOIDS the run regardless of its retrieval numbers. The enum is the kernel's published contract (openapi.yaml /recall 200.decision); a client-side third value is a contract lie, not a new state.

T3_abstention_reachable.rule: At least 1 of the 106 judged queries must return `decision: low_confidence` with zero passages.
T3_abstention_reachable.decides_in_advance: Zero abstentions is a FINDING that this corpus cannot support the abstention eval (Plan 08 §2.3) and that a dedicated abstention fixture is owed. It is explicitly NOT a pass. This is the arm that stops 'no abstentions observed' from being read as 'the abstention path is fine'.
T3_abstention_reachable.rationale: The fixture carries exactly one negation probe, so a zero here is plausible — which is exactly why the outcome had to be assigned before the number was known.

T4_refusal_is_not_absence.rule: Each run makes at least 1 deliberately unauthorized call. It must yield the refusal state, and that state's shape must be structurally distinguishable from an absence (empty passages with `decision: ok`).
T4_refusal_is_not_absence.decides_in_advance: A refusal and an absence may never share a rendered form. Collapsing them is a confidentiality leak (Plan 04 §5), so this is gated on STRUCTURE, not on styling and not on a count.
T4_refusal_is_not_absence.compares: outcome discriminant + presence of passages (structural), never a total

T5_recall_row.rule: Record recall@5 over the 106 judged queries, the per-query ordered hit ids, each decision, and the zero-hit query set. This row is the REFERENT, not a verdict.
T5_recall_row.decides_in_advance: Any future default-model swap is judged at ±3 points against THIS row (Plan 08 §2.1). No committed row, no swap — and because P3 is CLOSED, the rule is currently inert: it binds a future proposal, it does not license one.
T5_recall_row.why_not_gating: Gating it would make an unmeasured retrieval number a pass/fail criterion chosen after the fact, which is the failure Plan 08 §0 exists to prevent. The corpus is truncated (see dataset bounds), so its absolute value is not a quality claim.

T6_dataset_and_harness_drift.rule: The fixture sha256 above must match the fixture on disk at run time. A mismatch voids the baseline; it is re-taken, never silently re-baselined.
T6_dataset_and_harness_drift.decides_in_advance: Editing the fixture to make a number look good is the one move that destroys the only baseline this phase produces (Plan 08 §5).
